description.p: Lumux is a lightweight desktop app that analyzes the colors on your screen and streams them to a Philips Hue Entertainment area for an "ambilight" effect.
It is designed for Wayland desktops and uses the XDG Desktop Portal ScreenCast API (PipeWire) so you control when and what Lumux can capture.

ul.li: Hue Entertainment streaming (DTLS) for smooth, low-latency updates
Portal-based screen capture on Wayland (no privileged access required)
Configurable zone grid and real-time zone preview
Performance controls (resolution scale, target FPS, smoothing, gamma/brightness)
Optional tray integration and quick start/stop controls

description.p: Requires a Philips Hue Bridge and an Entertainment area configured in the Hue app.

screenshot.caption: Main application window with zone preview

ul.li: Brightness reaches the slider value: smoothing no longer stalls short of it, and dark-but-coloured scenes no longer dim the lights (only true black fades)
Shows the brightness Lumux is sending ("lights at N%") in the Decky panel and the window
Brightness is now the lights' own brightness: 100% = Hue's maximum whatever the screen shows, and the slider tunes it down; only near-black areas fade the lights out
Saturation 100% now lands exactly on the edge of Hue's colour range in every hue (computed in the lights' colour space)
Brightness slider goes to 100% = Hue's maximum (was 200%); lower values now dim proportionally
Saturation slider goes to 100% = the most vivid colours the lights can show (was 300%); 0% = as on screen; starts at 100%
Decky sliders no longer jump back after you move them
Desktop: brightness and saturation are live sliders in the main window
decky-lumux: Install Lumux from Game Mode. The plugin downloads the matching lumux.flatpak release and its GNOME runtime, with progress in the panel, so no Desktop Mode step is needed
decky-lumux: Update Lumux button when the installed Flatpak is older than the plugin
decky-lumux: the "Lumux not installed" state no longer sticks after (re)installing the Flatpak, so the bridge pairing option appears in Game Mode
decky-lumux: "Check again" button and the reason the Flatpak wasn't found
More vivid default: 100% saturation now equals the old 200%

Decky plugin uses the desktop app's settings: no second pairing, and pairing/slider changes save correctly (the plugin now reads and writes settings.json itself, since the Flatpak sandbox Decky starts may not see it)
Stopping sync (or quitting, or leaving Game Mode) no longer turns the lights off; they stay on their last synced colours
New Saturation slider (window and Decky panel) for more vivid colours
Brighter default: 100% brightness now equals the old 200%
Ask the screen-cast portal for shared-memory frames first; GPU buffer import could silently produce black frames (lights stuck at 1%)
Fall back to the next capture method automatically if a pipeline only produces black frames
Starting sync in the window stops the Decky background service if it is streaming, instead of fighting over the entertainment area
Start can no longer get stuck after a failed connection attempt
Lumux now writes a log file (~/.var/app/io.github.enginkirmaci.lumux/cache/lumux/lumux.log) and says where its settings file is
New headless lumux-daemon, controlled over a local socket, used by the Lumux Decky Loader plugin
Screen capture from gamescope's PipeWire output in Game Mode, without a screen-share dialog
Pair with the bridge from Game Mode by pressing its link button

description.p: Fixes screen capture on Wayland inside Flatpak (lights stayed dark): Lumux now connects to PipeWire through the screen-cast portal, warns when capture delivers no frames, and explains when X11 capture can't be used.

ul.li: Keep the entertainment session alive while screen capture starts, and reconnect automatically if the bridge drops it
Native DTLS streaming instead of an openssl subprocess, with a real handshake check
X11 screen capture, used automatically on X11 sessions such as SteamOS Desktop Mode
Streaming works right after pairing without restarting the app
Reading mode only controls lights in the selected entertainment area
Lower CPU use: unchanged frames are not re-analysed and frames are pulled at the sync rate
Handle padded row strides and avoid odd scaled widths in capture pipeline
Fall back to next converter on runtime pipeline errors for more resilient capture
Migrated image processing pipeline from PIL to numpy arrays for better memory efficiency
Added dynamic scale factor with automatic pipeline restart support
Pre-computed message buffers and encoded config ID at init for faster entertainment streaming
Converted bridge status checks to async with thread safety for settings application
Added bidirectional RGB/XY color conversion and migrated utils into the lumux package
Optimized zone preview to skip redraws when colors haven't changed
Tuned default sync performance: increased FPS to 30, reduced transition time to 50ms
Fixed Hue lights staying on after application or system shutdown
Fixed autostart toggle not persisting in Flatpak sandbox
Added SIGTERM signal handler for clean shutdown during system power off
Improved autostart file path detection in Flatpak environments
Added Reading Mode with configurable static color and brightness controls
Added automatic Reading Mode activation on startup
Improved Reading Mode responsiveness with debounced brightness updates and auto-apply behavior
Fixed autostart setup by creating the desktop entry directory automatically and handling Flatpak permission errors more gracefully
Added a capture source selector to sync either the entire screen or a single window
Improved capture cleanup so stopping sync also closes the active PipeWire portal session
Saved the selected capture source in settings so it persists across restarts
Added Bridge Setup Wizard with automatic discovery and authentication
Added black bar detection for letterbox/pillarbox video content
Replaced python-hue-v2 with unified BridgeClient for better reliability
Improved code structure and maintainability
Added autostart at login support for Flatpak
Fixed config persistence in Flatpak sandbox (now uses XDG_CONFIG_HOME)
Improved settings management for sandboxed environments

description.p: Initial release of Lumux for Philips Hue Sync.

ul.li: Hue Entertainment streaming with DTLS for smooth, low-latency light updates
Portal-based screen capture on Wayland using XDG Desktop Portal and PipeWire
Configurable zone grid with real-time preview
Performance controls including resolution scale, target FPS, smoothing, gamma, and brightness
System tray integration with quick start/stop controls
